items.definition:
art, objects, or design considered to be in poor taste
Her apartment was filled with kitsch from various souvenir shops.

a state of being drowsy and sluggish
The heat caused a feeling of lethargy throughout the afternoon.

the indispensable factor or influence that gives something its strength and vitality
Communication is the lifeblood of any successful relationship.

a powerful whirlpool; a state of confused movement or violent turmoil
The country was caught in a maelstrom of political unrest.

a gangster's female companion (informal, dated)
In old crime films, the gangster's moll often wore flashy clothes.

a mass of rocks and sediment carried and deposited by a glacier
The retreating glacier left behind a large terminal moraine.

opposition or opponent (informal)
He always tries to outsmart his oppo in negotiations.

great wealth or luxury
The palace was decorated with incredible opulence.

wild and noisy disorder or confusion
There was complete pandemonium in the hall after the announcement.

a person who spreads propaganda
The government employed a skilled propagandist to influence public opinion.

a heap of combustible material, especially one for burning a corpse
The ancient king's body was placed on a funeral pyre.

the tendency of a convicted criminal to reoffend
The program aims to reduce recidivism among former inmates.

the ability of a system to handle a growing amount of work
The new software offers improved scalability for large enterprises.

a state of being extremely dirty and unpleasant, especially as a result of poverty or neglect
The family was living in conditions of extreme squalor.

deceit used in order to achieve one's goal
He used subterfuge to gain access to the confidential files.

a substance that reduces the surface tension of a liquid
Surfactants are commonly used in detergents and soaps.

the process of determining the location of a point by forming triangles
GPS uses triangulation to pinpoint your exact location.

energy and enthusiasm
He approached the task with great vim and vigor.

an affair; a scandalous or controversial incident
The whole affaire became a public scandal.

a drug acting to relieve pain
The doctor prescribed an analgesic for the pain.

a person who has ambitions to achieve something, typically to follow a particular career
She is an aspirant to a career in medicine.

a large, heavy, single-edged knife, especially one used in the Philippines
The farmer used a bolo to clear the brush.

a tall fur hat, typically worn by soldiers
The guard wore a distinctive busby on his head.

a window or part of a window set on a hinge
She opened the casement window to let in the fresh air.

an underground pit or tank for receiving and temporarily storing sewage and wastewater
The old house had a cesspool instead of a modern septic system.

an official of the Communist Party responsible for political education and organization
The political commissar ensured party loyalty within the ranks.

a small dome, especially one covering a circular or polygonal opening in a roof or ceiling
The old building was topped with a decorative cupola.

a ruler with absolute power, typically one who exercises it in a cruel or oppressive way
The country was ruled by a cruel despot for decades.

a device, circuit, transducer, or program that converts information from one format or code to another
The video encoder compresses the raw footage.

the great or extreme scale, seriousness, or extent of something perceived as bad or morally wrong
The enormity of the crime shocked the nation.

a person or thing serving as a typical example or excellent model
She was an exemplar of dedication and hard work.

a lively Spanish dance; a foolish or useless act or thing
The party turned into a real fandango with everyone dancing.

a flour or meal made from cereal grains, especially wheat, used in puddings or as a breakfast cereal
She made a hot breakfast cereal from farina.

strict adherence to prescribed forms or rules
The artist rejected strict formalism in favor of free expression.

localized death and decomposition of body tissue
The doctor warned that without treatment, gangrene could set in.

habitual greed or excess in eating
Gluttony is considered one of the seven deadly sins.

grain that is to be ground
All his experiences were grist for his writing.

low blood sugar
Symptoms of hypoglycemia include dizziness and confusion.

underactive thyroid gland
Hypothyroidism can cause fatigue and weight gain.

a male relative
He traveled far to visit his kinsman.

the removal or loosening of restrictions
The government announced the liberalisation of trade policies.

the branch of economics concerned with large-scale or general economic factors
Students in economics often study both microeconomics and macroeconomics.

a legislative assembly or council in some Islamic countries
The Majlis approved the new budget.

Relating to the geological era from about 252 to 66 million years ago, characterized by the dominance of dinosaurs
Dinosaurs roamed the Earth during the Mesozoic Era.

a green or brown film on the surface of bronze or similar metals, produced by oxidation over a long period.
The old bronze statue had a beautiful green patina.

the doctrine that knowledge, truth, and morality exist in relation to culture, society, or historical context, and are not absolute.
Cultural relativism suggests that moral standards vary between societies.

the principles or policy of the Republican party; the principles of a republican government.
American republicanism emphasizes civic virtue and popular sovereignty.

restaurant owner
The restaurateur greeted every guest personally.

sacred things; sacred rites
The ancient texts describe the sacra of the temple.

a member of any of the peoples who speak or spoke a Semitic language
Hebrew is a Semitic language, spoken by Semites.

a person who publicizes or praises something or someone for reasons of self-interest, personal profit, or ulterior motive
The influencer was accused of being a shill for the product.

a cylindrical coil of wire acting as a magnet when carrying electric current
The car's starter motor uses a solenoid.

an operational flight by a single aircraft
The fighter jet completed its reconnaissance sortie.

an act of undressing to music
The club featured a nightly striptease show.

a member of the ancient non-Semitic people of Sumer
The Sumerian civilization developed cuneiform writing.

dramatic behavior or theatrical effects
The play was full of dramatic theatrics.

the state of living in tribes or strong loyalty to one's own tribe or social group
The rise of tribalism can lead to conflict.

the final or eventual outcome or conclusion of a discussion, action, or series of events
The upshot of the meeting was a decision to proceed with the plan.

an increase or surge
There has been an upsurge in demand for renewable energy.

a person who gains sexual pleasure from watching others
The police arrested the voyeur who was peeking into windows.

an area of open country, typically undulating or hilly
The sheep grazed peacefully on the green wold.

a class of naturally occurring organic compounds
Morphine is a well-known alkaloid derived from opium.

a person who abandons a religious or political belief
He was declared an apostate after publicly renouncing his faith.

axon
An axon is a long, slender projection of a nerve cell.
